questions.prompt: What happens when you build this?

context.label: post-grid.component.ts

code.label: post-grid.component.html
code.source: @for (post of posts; track post.id) { }

options.text: The build fails: `posts` is a signal, which can't be looped over
It builds, and the grid is empty
It works: Angular reads signals in `@for` automatically

questions.explanation: An input is a signal, and a signal is a function. Call it: `@for (post of posts(); track post.id)`.

questions.prompt: Code review: some lines of this template don't work as intended. Click every one of them.

context.label: post-card.component.ts

code.label: post-card.component.html
code.source: @if (isLiked) { } @for (comment of comments(); track comment.id) { } {{ post().likes }} likes

questions.explanation: Line 2 passes the signal itself instead of the post: `[post]="post()"`. Line 3 checks the signal function, which is always truthy: `@if (isLiked())`. Line 6 only refers to the method and never calls it: `(click)="like()"`. The `@for` and the like count are fine.

questions.prompt: The parent opens and closes the comment form with `[(isOpen)]`, and the form can close itself. What goes in the gap?

code.label: comment-form.component.ts

questions.explanation: `model()` is an input the component can also write to: `set` updates it, and the change goes back to the parent through `[(isOpen)]`. An `input()` is read-only, so `set` doesn't build. A plain `signal()` can't be bound from the parent.

questions.prompt: What happens when you build this?

options.text: The build fails: `posts()` can be `undefined` until the request answers
It builds and shows "0 posts" until the data arrives
It builds, and `toSignal` waits for the data before the page renders

questions.explanation: Without `initialValue`, `toSignal` starts as `undefined`, so its type is `Post[] | undefined` and strict templates reject `.length`. Pass `{ initialValue: [] }`, or write `posts()?.length`.

questions.prompt: The feed should be sorted by likes. This throws in development, because the array belongs to the store. Which version fixes it?

code.label: feed-page.component.ts

questions.explanation: `[...]` copies the array, and only the copy is sorted. Without the copy, `sort` still changes the store's frozen array, so moving it into a `computed` throws the same error. A signal from `selectSignal` is read-only, so `set` doesn't build: the state only changes through actions.

questions.prompt: The posts reducer sets `status: 'loading'` on `loadFeed`. The server is down. What does the user see?

code.label: posts.effects.ts

options.text: A spinner that never stops: no failure action is dispatched, so the status stays `loading`
An error message from the store

questions.explanation: Without `catchError`, the error only reaches the console. Nothing tells the reducer the request failed. Add `catchError((error: HttpErrorResponse) => of(PostsActions.loadFeedFailure({ errorMessage: error.message })))` inside the inner pipe.

questions.explanation: Reading the error before searching for it saves a lot of time. Each of these has come up in an earlier quiz: they are the mistakes almost everyone makes once.

questions.prompt: A trainee writes `::ng-deep .p-dialog { border-radius: 8px; }` in the post card's SCSS. What does it do?

options.text: It becomes a global rule and changes every dialog in the app, not only the post card's
It changes only the dialog inside the post card

questions.explanation: `::ng-deep` turns off encapsulation for that rule, so it leaks to every component. Angular strongly discourages it. Use the preset, `[dt]`, or a CSS variable on your own element.
